reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes unusually rapid cryptocurrency returns, claiming that 0.3 BNB produced over 10.7 BNB and showing an apparent balance of 10.793 BNB. It connects the return claim to deploying a contract, adding liquidity, and transferring at least 0.5 BNB or 0.15 ETH to a contract or bot address, with larger deposits described as offering greater potential profit. The variable-return qualification and educational disclaimer provide limitations but do not remove the promotional money-and-return flow.

citations.quote: In this video, you can see how I used Flash loan to Arbitrage in Binance Mainnet or Ethereum Mainnet by deploying Contract/Token to mask our arbitrage attack.
Deposit funds (at least 0.5 BNB or 0.15 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
This can be any amount from 1000 and up.
Here I will choose 0.3 BNB.
We are going to execute the flash loan attack.

opening.argument: Judge the return claim alongside the speaker's limits on it. The narration says outcomes differ with network volume and liquidity, including cases with only a small return. It also acknowledges that the process may not work or produce a large profit. The closing screen warns viewers to prevent losses and says the material is for educational purposes. Those qualifications do not prove the demonstration is sound, but they weigh against reading the large displayed result as a guaranteed payout to every viewer.

citations.quote: Now remember, the return is different every time depending on the network volume and the amount of liquidity you put in. Sometimes you will get a small amount, while other times you can hit it big like we did here.
If it doesn't work or you don't get a large profit, try depositing a different amount of liquidity in your contract

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the 0.3 BNB example and the funding instructions as a promise of the same return to viewers. But the speaker explicitly says returns vary and can be small; the closing warning even acknowledges possible losses. A required funding amount may be consequential, but these passages do not establish a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: Sometimes you will get a small amount, while other times you can hit it big like we did here.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not change what viewers are urged to do. The description promises daily earnings in its headline, then directs them to deposit BNB or ETH to a contract or bot address. The narration reinforces that flow with an extraordinary claimed gain in minutes. Saying results vary does not neutralize the funding-and-returns pitch.

citations.quote: EARN 10 BNB or 5 Ethereum Per DAY Passive | EASY - 10X - Huge Profits
Deposit funds (at least 0.5 BNB or 0.15 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
I used just 0.3 BNB to gain over 10.7 BNB in just minutes.

opening.argument: The material walks through an operational process: setting up a wallet, creating a Solidity file, compiling it, and connecting the wallet to a deployed contract. The speaker explains that the wallet connection enables interaction with the contract, while the description defines a flash loan's repayment constraint. That sequence supports reading the video as a technical demonstration with a claimed example result, not merely an invitation to hand money to someone else. The result still needs scrutiny, but the detailed workflow matters when deciding the video's primary character.

citations.quote: Before you get started, you need to make sure you have the MetaMask wallet installed on your internet browser.
Now you want to paste in the smart contract code. Into this new file. I'll put the newest updated code in the video description.
This will connect your MetaMask browser wallet if it isn't connected already so that you. Can interact with the contract.
A flash loan has to be borrowed and repaid within the same blockchain transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes the deployment and deposit steps as though their presence settles the video's purpose. Yet those steps sit within instructions to compile code, connect a wallet, and interact with a newly created contract. The quoted loan amount is an input in that walkthrough, not proof by itself that a viewer is paying an identified operator. The apparent balance is a demonstrated outcome, not independent verification of how it arose.

citations.quote: Then go down and click compile. Once that's done, go over to the third tab on the left.
This will connect your MetaMask browser wallet if it isn't connected already so that you. Can interact with the contract.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical steps can be the vehicle for a financial solicitation. Here the walkthrough directs viewers to copy linked code, deploy it, fund the resulting contract or bot address, and start it. The same description advertises large daily profits. The explanation of flash loans does not verify the supplied code or establish that the depicted balance came from arbitrage.

citations.quote: Click the link below then Copy and Paste the code in Remix:
Deposit funds (at least 0.5 BNB or 0.15 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
EARN 10 BNB or 5 Ethereum Per DAY Passive | EASY - 10X - Huge Profits

opening.argument: The funding step is described as adding liquidity to a newly created contract, with the viewer told to copy that contract's address. The description even calls it 'your own BOT' and refers to a withdrawal control. Those details leave an important gap in a claim that viewers are sending funds to a scam operator: the supplied material does not identify a third-party recipient or show who controls the linked code. Nor does the speaker promise a fixed return; the narration says it can be small. This may be a risky or unverified trading workflow, but the shown deposit alone does not establish a diversion of funds.

citations.quote: click to copy the contract address. You are now going to add liquidity to make your new token have a value you can actually trade against.
After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now
'withdrawal' Share your profits in the comments section below.
Sometimes you will get a small amount, while other times you can hit it big like we did here.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly points to a deposit, but its quoted instruction calls the destination 'your exact contract/bot address'; the narration likewise says to copy the newly created contract address. Neither passage identifies the contract's controller or shows funds reaching the presenter. The 0.3 BNB example and variable loan amount show what is entered or claimed, not that a particular third party receives the deposit.

click to copy the contract address.
Here I will choose 0.3 BNB.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The recipient need not be identified for the video's funding-and-returns pitch to be concerning. Viewers are instructed to copy externally linked code, deploy it, and fund the contract before starting the bot. Calling it 'your own BOT' does not establish who controls what that code does. The claimed gain of over 10 BNB within minutes supplies the incentive to follow those instructions, while the provided material does not independently verify that return.
